lines.li: [them] Our people are giving up {SITUATIONPLACE}, and the families are already on the road.
[us] What happened there?
[them,their:tribal] Too many bad moons, and the elders said the place had turned against us.
[them] Too little left to keep the families, and the families have stopped hoping it will mend.
[us] I'm sorry.
[them] So are they, most of them were born there.
[us] Where will the families from {SITUATIONPLACE} go?
[them,their:tribal] To our other hearths, with whatever they can carry on their backs.
[them,their:medieval] To kin in our other towns, mostly, with their carts piled to the sky.
[them,their:spacer] To our other settlements, wherever the habitats have room for them.
[them] To our other towns, mostly, wherever there's room and work.
[us] I hope they find it.
[them] Some will, the young ones always do.
[them] What doesn't fit on the carts at {SITUATIONPLACE} is being left behind.
[us] Left for anyone?
[them] Doors and pots and an old forge, for whoever comes with a cart of their own.
[them] We heard you did right by the families from {SITUATIONPLACE} on the road.
[us] It was little enough.
[them] It was more than most did.
[them] I remember when {SITUATIONPLACE} was a place people walked a day to see.
[us] What was it like?
[them] Loud, and full, and nothing like it is now.
[them] Our people are leaving {SITUATIONPLACE}, so you'll forgive me if I'm short.
[us] Of course.
[them] Most of the families from the town we gave up have found new roofs now.
[us] And the town?
[them,their:tribal] Cold hearths, mostly, and the grass coming back in.
[them,their:hightech] Empty streets, mostly, and the weather getting into everything.
[them] Empty houses, mostly, and the weather moving in.
[them] We've only just moved into the old walls at {TOWN}, the place is still half rubble.
[us] Was much left?
[them,their:tribal] Hearthstones, and a lodge post with marks none of us can read.
[them,their:medieval] Good stone, a sound well, and a hall roof that wants patching.
[them,their:industrial] The foundations, the water lines, and a great deal of broken glass.
[them,their:spacer] The habitat frames were sound, but not one of the seals was.
[them] More than you'd think, and less than we hoped.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {PEOPLE} have settled the old walls of {TOWN}.

lines.li: [us] Why settle a ruin?
[them] The walls were already there, and walls are the hard part.
[us] Aren't you afraid it'll go the same way?
[them,their:tribal] The spirits of a place forget, if you give them time.
[them] Whatever drove the others off, we're not them.
[them] The household has taken up the old site at {TOWN}, and will put it in proper order.
[us] Was it imperial before?
[them] It is now, which is what matters to the court.
[them] My children slept in a house with no door our first night at {TOWN}, and loved it.
[us] And you?
[them,their:lowtech] I sat up by the doorway with a spear, and loved it less.
[them] I sat up by the doorway with a rifle, and loved it less.
[them,their:tribal] Our new hearth at {TOWN} burns where an older one did, we found its stones.
[them,their:medieval] We raised {TOWN} on old foundations, and the masons say they beat ours.
[them,their:hightech] {TOWN} went up on an old site, which saved us a season of digging.
[them] {TOWN} stands where an older town stood, and we used every stone it left.
[us] Do you know who lived there?
[them] Only what the walls tell us, and walls don't say much.
[them] Some of the old folk at {TOWN} won't walk the old streets after dark.
[us] Afraid of ghosts?
[them] Afraid of tripping, mostly, the old streets are all holes.
[them] I lost one home when our old town was given up, and I'm building another at {TOWN}.
[us] Is it the same?
[them,their:tribal] No hearth is the same, but the fire is.
[them] Nothing's the same, but a roof is a roof.
[them] We each brought one thing from the old town, and they're all on one shelf at {TOWN}.
[us] What did you bring?
[them,their:tribal] A carved bone from the old lodge door, for luck.
[them] A door key, for a door that isn't there anymore.
[them] We've lost one town already, so don't expect cheerful neighbors.
[us] We don't.
